rows.speaker: الفلاسفة التناسخية
rows.claim: Biqaʿi rejects the view of transmigrationist philosophers who say souls leave bodies at death for celestial beings or realms and have no further bodily attachment or resurrection.
rows.anchor: من الفلاسفة التناسخية وغيرهم ممن يقر بالوحدانية من يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings live in this earth first and again, in both outward and inward life as bodies and souls; the verse excludes another earthly realm.
rows.anchor: أي أولا وثانيا على ما أنتم عليه بظواهركم وبواطنكم ابدانا وأرواحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People die in this earth as a whole, yet souls retain some connection to bodies, allowing the dead to answer the angels in the grave and bodies to feel pleasure or pain.
rows.anchor: أي من الحياة الأولى بجملتكم فيكون للارواح تعلق بالأبدان بوجه ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead emerge from this earth as body and soul after returning to dust, to be requited and to manifest God's justice by restoring rights among people.
rows.anchor: أي روحا وبدنا بعد موتكم فيها وعودكم إلى ما كنتم عليه أولا ترابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affirmation of resurrection concludes the story by returning to the afterlife message with which it began.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على الحشر فذلكة القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account confirms that persistent sin is the community's habit, continuing the account of their Sabbath transgression in 7:163.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر أن الفسق ديدنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioning group is a community of righteous admonishers who had persisted in warning until they despaired of another group that would not desist.
rows.anchor: جماعة ممن يعتبر ويقصد من الواعظين الصالحين الذين وعظوا حتى أيسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners ask why they keep admonishing people expected to be destroyed or severely punished for their persistent corruption.
rows.anchor: لا يقلعون عن الوعظ تخوفا للموعوظين بما ينجاوزن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonishers answer that they warn to have an excuse before their Lord: if asked about the sinners, they can say they made every effort.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليكم بالحفظ عما وقعوا فيه من الذنب والإقبال على الوعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their other hope is that the warnings might make the sinners fear God and turn back from their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وليكون حالهم حال من يرجى خوفه لله فيرجع عن غيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the sinners failed to return, God fulfilled the warning by bringing both severe punishment and destruction upon them.
rows.anchor: أخبر أنه صدق ظنهم بإيقاع الأمرين معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forgetting means they acted as if forgetful, abandoning the warning that God would not leave them free to do as they pleased.
rows.anchor: فعلوا في اعراضهم عنه فعل الناسي وتركوه ترك المنسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved those who continued to forbid evil.
rows.anchor: الذين ينهون } أي استمروا على النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers received a very severe punishment because they kept renewing their sinful conduct.
rows.anchor: بعذاب بئيس * } أي شديد جدا

words: فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا عَنْ مَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the severe punishment they grew arrogant and defiant, advanced into other sins, and became hardened against admonition and its deterrent effect.
rows.anchor: أي تكبروا جلافة ويبسا عن الانتهاء

rows.speaker: عبد الحق
rows.claim: Biqaʿi cites ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq's lexicon al-Wāhī for the gloss that the rebellious person advances in all his affairs; he also gives other glosses for the word.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الحق في كتابة الواهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported glosses for ʿatā are to go to excess in committing sins, or to be so rebellious that admonition and warning no longer benefit the person.
rows.anchor: العاتي هو المبالغ في ركوب المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to the reformers contrasts with the preceding corruptors, who falsified claims about God and spoiled the book; Biqaʿi connects the righteous to the community in 7:159.
rows.anchor: بين ما للمفسدين من كونهم قالوا على الله غير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Holding the book means clinging to it continuously and firmly, a difficult commitment especially when corruption is widespread, so they do not falsely speak about God.
rows.anchor: يمسكون إمساكا شديدا يتجدد على كل وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True adherence to a revealed book includes leaving it for its abrogating successor, since the earlier book itself testifies to the abrogation.
rows.anchor: ومن جملة تمسيكهم المتجدد انتقالهم عن ذلك الكتاب عند إتيان الناسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi explains the past-tense wording for prayer as preventing the former community from using its established prayer as an argument to remain in its old religion.
rows.anchor: عبر عن إقامة الصلاة المعهودة لهم بلفظ الماضي دون المضارع لئلا يجعلوه حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out because earlier people had abandoned it, as stated in the verse in Maryam, and because it is one of religion's greatest rites.
rows.anchor: وخصها إشارة إلى أن الأولين توكوها كما صرح به في آية مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise generalizes the reward to all reformers and assures that none of their recompense will be lost in any way.
rows.anchor: وضع موضعه للتعميم قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning and inviting through the book, the passage recalls a past earthly punishment so they will take the covenant seriously; the Prophet's knowledge of it despite being unlettered is a manifest sign of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: أمره أن يذكرهم بترهيب دنيوي مضى إيقاعه بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to uproot and raise; the majestic plural intensifies the warning.
rows.anchor: وأتى بنون العظمة لزيادة الترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain is definite because the audience knows it; Biqaʿi prefers al-jabal to al-ṭūr here because its wording conveys hardship and severity fitting their heedlessness.
rows.anchor: عبر لدلالة لفظه على الصعوبة والشدة دون الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's majesty and power, Biqaʿi again discredits false gods, stressing their utter incapacity and contrasting true worship with worship of idols.
rows.anchor: كرر التنفير عن أندادهم في أسلوب آخر تأكيدا للمعنى السابق بزيادة بالغة في العجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that people persistently call on the idols apart from God, or that they call on the idols while leaving God.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يدعونه سبحانه في بعض الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot help their worshippers in any way, while God alone has power over them.
rows.anchor: أي بوجه من وجوه النصرة بدليل عجزكم عني وأنا وحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot defend even themselves; a dog can urinate on them and they cannot stop it.
rows.anchor: بدليل أن الكلب يبول عليهم فلا يمنعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a group calling is more likely to be heard than one person's call, the idols still do not hear even an invitation to the noblest quality, guidance.
rows.anchor: ولما كان دعاء الجماعة أقرب إلى السماع من دعاء الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols seem to look at the Prophet, but their apparent gaze is not sight.
rows.anchor: ينظرون إليك } أي نوعا من الإبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi compares the Qur'anic argument with Isaiah's denunciation of idols, which declares God alone eternal and describes idols and their makers as unable to see, hear, or know.
rows.anchor: وما أشبه مضمون هذه الآيات بما في سفر أنبياء بني إسرائيل في نبوة أشعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the appeal for refuge and may answer it, knows both the person's intention and the enemy's, and nothing can overcome Him.
rows.anchor: فهو يسمع استعاذتك فيجيبك إن شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hearing and knowledge were already explicitly denied of the idols, God's affirmation of these attributes suffices without an exclusive formula; Biqaʿi contrasts wording in 41:36.
rows.anchor: صار إثبات ذلك له كافيا في اختصاصه به من غير حاجه إلى الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both this passage and Fussilat end with God's knowledge because satanic whispering is hidden; Ghafir instead ends with sight because some human threats are visible.
rows.anchor: وختم بصفة العلم في الموضعين لأن الوسوسة من باب ما يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording signals that the Prophet experiences only a slight satanic prompting, while the uncertainty particle indicates it is not firmly established; refuge should be sought at its first onset.
rows.anchor: شيء خفيف جدا كما نبه عليه بالنزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic statement about the God-fearing explains the command to seek refuge and contrasts its confirmation with the earlier singular address to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وحقق أذاه لهم باداة التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāʾif can be an active participle like mayyit or māʾit, or a verbal noun; the image is Satan circling them and never leaving.
rows.anchor: على أنه فاعل كميت ومائت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's circuit sometimes affects them, even surrounding them from every side, and sometimes passes without effect; Satan is far from mercy and burned by the curse.
rows.anchor: فيكون قد مسهم مسا هو أكبر من النزع لكونه أطاف بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They make themselves remember God and whatever benefits them in both acting and refraining.
rows.anchor: كلفوا أنفسهم ذكر الله بجيع ما ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal clause and suddenness particle portray immediate, stable insight from the light of the heart, so they do not follow Satan.
rows.anchor: أشاره إلى ذلك بالجملة الاسمية مؤكدا لسرعة البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing person desires but restrains himself and sees but refrains; one who persists with Satan becomes blind through wrongdoing, as if in darkness.
rows.anchor: فإن المتقي من يشتهي فينتهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This points to what God has revealed, which should remain present in people's minds and before their eyes.
rows.anchor: مشيرا إلى ما يوحي إليه تنبيها على أنه يجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is the choicest response to their request, enlightening hearts and eyes to see signs and acquire knowledge they lacked.
rows.anchor: أي أشياء هي - على حسب ما طلبتم - مجتباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives reason insight into proofs of God's oneness, prophethood, resurrection, and the whole of religious teaching; it names the cause, insight, for its effect.
rows.anchor: وسماه بذلك لأنه سبب لبصر العقول بدلائل التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the revelation to their Lord recalls His unceasing beneficence and makes it fitting that they receive what comes from Him graciously.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لم يقطع إحسانه عنكم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is clarification, while mercy adds the further meaning of gracious favor.
rows.anchor: لما كان البيان قد لا يكون على وجه الإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are those who realize the truth of faith and renew it continually; for others the revelation may instead become a punishment.
rows.anchor: أي يوجدون هذه الحقيقة ويستمرون على تجديدها في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recited Qur'an is the revelation just described and the attribute of their Lord, so listeners should approach it humbly and with proper courtesy.
rows.anchor: فتأدبوا وتواضعوا لأنه صفة ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening requires directing one's ears to the recitation and making an effort to avoid distractions.
rows.anchor: ألقوا إليه أسماعكم مجتهدين في عدم شاغل يشغلكم عن السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent ruling requires everyone to be silent for every reciter; Biqaʿi urges silence because the Qur'an merits undivided attention.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية وجوب الإنصات لكل قارئ على كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silence enables reflection and deliberation, unveiling the heart so listeners understand and act on the Qur'an without inward resistance.
rows.anchor: للتأمل والتدبر لتنجلي قلوبكم فتعلموا حقيقة فتعلموا بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command offers hope that God will honor the listeners as a merciful person treats the recipient of mercy.
rows.anchor: لتكون على رجاء من أن يكرمكم ربكم ويفعل بكم كل ما يفعله الراحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command moves from remembering God at Satan's prompting to listening to the Qur'an, the greatest remembrance, and applies reading etiquette in every situation.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم الأمر بالذكر عند نزغ الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciter may raise his voice to gain listeners or recite quietly to avoid obliging others to listen; the command covers both cases.
rows.anchor: وربما أسر لئلا يوجب على غيره الإصغاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts from the audience to their leader, the Prophet, to encourage their acceptance and suggest that he alone can fully carry out this duty.
rows.anchor: ورقي الخطاب منهم إلى إمامهم ليكون أدعى لقبولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble the deaf who do not benefit from hearing, the mute who do not speak beneficially, and people without reason who do not use it.
rows.anchor: مشابهة لحال الأصم في عدم السماع لعدم الانتفاع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are classed among earthly creatures, even beasts, and made the worst of them, with the judgment measured by God's all-encompassing knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: جعلهم من جنس الحشرات أو البهائم ثم جعلهم شرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no reason that develops; anyone who fails to benefit from the caller is likewise without effective understanding.
rows.anchor: أي لا يتجدد لهم عقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says God formed them from the outset with a deeply corrupt disposition, like an incorrigible scorpion, knew there was no good in them, and left them to that known state.
rows.anchor: وجعل جواهرهم شريرة كجوهر العقرب التي لا تقبل التأديب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearing God would grant is the kind that brings a lasting response; because God's knowledge encompasses all, the absence of known good here means there is no good in them.
rows.anchor: وهو ما تعقبه الإجابة المستمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if God forced them to answer while they remained unreceptive, they would turn away afterward and not sustain the response because their nature inclines to evil.
rows.anchor: إسماعا قسرهم فيه على الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi compares their reversal to apostates who entered Islam from fear of the sword or desire for money and then were killed after reverting.
rows.anchor: لأهل الردة الذين قتلوا مرتدين بعد أن كانوا دخلوا في الإسلام خوفا من السيف ورغبة في المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterfactual links to 6:28, where people returned to their former conduct after being sent back.
rows.anchor: ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge has four kinds: existing things, nonexistent things, how existing things would be if absent, and how nonexistent things would be if present; the verse concerns the fourth.
rows.anchor: فإن علم الله تعالى أربعة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says he encountered a person who exemplified the hypothetical: bold in falsehood and attack, but cowardly when summoned to truth and quick to retreat after trying to approach it.
rows.anchor: أجرأ الناس على الباطل , وأثبتهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi allows lo to attach a consequence to a condition whose opposite is more fitting: if they turn away even after hearing and answering, their turning away without those prompts is more likely.
rows.anchor: نبه على ذلك الرازي , ويحتمل

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Biqaʿi illustrates that conditional usage with ʿUmar's praise of Suhayb: even without fearing God, Suhayb would not disobey Him.
rows.anchor: عمر رضي الله عنه : نعم العبد صهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, lo keeps its ordinary counterfactual sense, with both clauses negated; the denied turning away is only the additional rejection caused by divinely enabled hearing.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون على بابها من أن الجزءين بعدها منفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second reading, the meaning is that if God enabled them to hear they would increase their rejection; this does not conflict with their actual stubborn refusal.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : ولو أسمعهم لزادوا إعراضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the disbelievers' punishment followed from refusing to respond, believers are told to answer so they do not share the disbelievers' fate at the gathering.
rows.anchor: ما مضى من نكال الكافرين مسببا عن عدم الاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address identifies them as people who have professed faith with their tongues.
rows.anchor: أي أقروا بالإيمان بألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must make their professed faith real by responding eagerly and wholeheartedly to God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: صدقوا دعواكم ذلك بإيجاد الإجابة إيجاد من هو في غاية الرغبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger was sent to all creation and only calls them to what God commands and to right guidance and good.
rows.anchor: وكان سبحانه لا يدعون إلا إلى صلاح ورشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lam instead of ilā signals how near the benefit of obedience is; the call gives moral life through faith and knowledge instead of the disbelievers' deafness, muteness, and lack of reason.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اجتناء ثمرة الطاعة في غاية القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is not confined to initial belief or some religious duties; the cited reports apply the call to answer even while praying.
rows.anchor: فلم تجد فيما أوحي الله إلي أن

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد ابن المعلى
rows.claim: In a report in Bukhari's tafsir and elsewhere, Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla was praying and delayed answering the Prophet until he finished; the Prophet cited this verse, then taught him that al-Fatiha is the greatest sura, the seven oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an given to him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد ابن المعلى رضي الله عنه قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Hurayra that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb delayed answering the Prophet while praying; the Prophet cited the verse, and Ubayy promised not to repeat this. The report is graded hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: وللترمذي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The same report says the Prophet offered to teach Ubayy a sura unmatched in Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an; Ubayy recited Umm al-Qur'an, and the Prophet identified it as the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur'an given to him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه ( أن النبي

words: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can return each person to the state He knows in them: an apparent believer may become a defiant unbeliever, while an unbeliever may be led back to faith.
rows.anchor: فيرده إلى ما علم منه فيصير فيما كشفه الحال كافرا معاندا بعد أن كان في ظاهر الحال مؤمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase's necessary closeness is a metonym for God's complete power to change people's intentions and desires.
rows.anchor: فكنى سبحانه بشدة القرب اللازم للحيلولة عن شدة الاقتدار على تبديل العزائم والمرادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should hasten to follow the Messenger while their hearts remain open to obedience, fearing that God may change their hearts.
rows.anchor: وهو تحريض على المبادرة إلى اتباع الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns them about their final return to God after warning them about the outcome of their present state.
rows.anchor: ولما خوفهم عاقبة الحال , حذرهم شأن المآل
